body.title: fix: misc improvements
body.body:
- Keep an `ImageOS` the job image or env sets, else derive it from the job's Ubuntu release, falling back to `ubuntu24` for `ubuntu-latest`
- Evaluate steps after a job timeout as cancelled, so `cancelled()` and `always()` cleanup runs
- Record nested reusable workflow results and forward their outputs
- Pass `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITEA_TOKEN` to called workflows by default

| Package | Type | Update | Change |

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>gitea/cli</summary>

### [`v1.2.0`](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/releases/tag/v1.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0)

gt 1.2.0 adds commands for commits, tags, activity feeds, stopwatches and branch protection rules, more of the `gh` options on the pull request, release, run and api commands, and makes commands run inside a clone about twice as fast.

##### Features

- `gt commit` reads commits on the server with `list`, `view`, `diff`, `compare`, `status` and `pr`, where a ref is a SHA, branch or tag. `status` exits 1 when a status failed and 8 while one is pending, so `gt commit status main && deploy` waits for green ([#​92](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/92)).
- `gt commit diff` and `gt pr diff` filter a diff with `--path` and `--exclude`, which take a file, a `dir/` or a glob and can be repeated, and summarize it with `--name-only`, `--name-status` and `--stat`. What is left is still a diff that `git apply` takes ([#​92](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/92)).
- `gt tag` lists, views, creates and deletes tags without a clone, and `protect`, `unprotect` and `protection list` manage tag protection rules. `create --message` makes an annotated tag ([#​93](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/93)).
- `gt branch protection list` and `view` show the protection rules in the order Gitea applies them: the approvals, who may push, the status checks and the other protections that are on ([#​95](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/95)).
- `gt activity [<owner>]` shows the activity feed of a user or organization, yours without an owner, and `gt repo activity` that of a repository. `--date` keeps one day and `--only-performed-by` keeps what the user did ([#​100](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/100)).
- `gt time start`, `stop`, `cancel` and `status` work with the issue stopwatch. `stop` logs the elapsed time, `cancel` discards it and `status` lists every active stopwatch across repositories ([#​101](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/101)).
- `gt pr merge --admin` merges past the branch protection, for those who administer the repository. `--match-head-commit SHA` merges only while the head is still that commit, and `--disable-auto` cancels the merge that `--auto` scheduled ([#​97](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/97)).
- `gt pr checks --required` shows and awaits only the checks that the protection rule of the base branch requires, so a flaky optional check no longer holds `--watch` back ([#​97](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/97)).
- `gt pr create --fill-first` takes the title and body from the first commit of the branch, and `--fill-verbose` takes the body from the full message of every commit ([#​97](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/97)).
- `gt release list` takes `--exclude-drafts`, `--exclude-pre-releases` and `--order asc|desc`, which sorts by when the releases were published ([#​98](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/98)).
- `gt run view --log-failed` prints the logs of the jobs that failed or were canceled, and `--job NAME|ID` views one job or, with `--log`, prints its log ([#​98](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/98)).
- `gt api --paginate --slurp` prints the pages as one JSON array, so a script parses one document ([#​98](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/98)).

##### Performance

- Commands run inside a clone are about twice as fast: `gt pr status`, `gt pr view`, `gt pr checks` and `gt status` take roughly half the time. Git is asked once per command instead of up to 11 times, and list pages and independent searches are read concurrently ([#​103](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/103)).

##### Fixes

- `gt upgrade --nightly` and the nightly option of the install scripts no longer fail with a checksum mismatch or install an old build. Nightly builds are now published to `gitea-cli/main-nightly`, which is not cached for a year. The 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 binaries still look in the old location, so upgrade to 1.2.0 before using `--nightly` again ([#​102](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/102)).
- On Windows, gt no longer fails to read its settings while another gt process is writing them ([#​105](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/105)).

##### Documentation

- The README lists the official `gitea-cli` package in the Arch Linux extra repository: `sudo pacman -S gitea-cli` ([#​96](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/96)).

##### Internal

- Integration tests cover `gt runner`, `gt gpg-key`, locking, pinning, deleting, dependencies, `--template` and `--dry-run` on a real Gitea ([#​94](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/94)).
- The golangci-lint configuration matches Gitea's, and `make fmt` runs `golangci-lint fmt` ([#​104](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/104)).
- Update `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` to v2.1.1, which includes a security fix for terminal size reports, and `github.com/itchyny/gojq` to v0.12.20 ([#​107](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/107)).
- Fix a flaky test that counted requests during concurrent page reads ([#​106](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/106)).

##### Contributors

- [@​lunny](https://github.com/lunny)
- [@​bircni](https://github.com/bircni)
- [@​silverwind](https://github.com/silverwind)
- [@​TheFox0x7](https://github.com/TheFox0x7)

**Full Changelog**: [v1.1.0...v1.2.0](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0)

### [`v1.1.0`](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/releases/tag/v1.1.0)

[Compare Source](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0)

gt 1.1.0 adds a preview for almost every change, Go templates for output, a machine-readable list of JSON fields, and new commands for GPG keys, issues, pull requests and administration.
There are no breaking changes.
gt still supports Gitea 28 and newer; a command that needs a newer Gitea now says so before sending any request ([#​67](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/67)).

##### Features

- `--dry-run` shows the write requests a command would send, without sending them, on about 149 commands: every command that only changes Gitea. Reads still go through, secrets are shown as `[REDACTED]`, and `--json` prints the requests as a report. Commands that also change the local clone or gt's settings, such as `gt pr create` and `gt repo clone`, don't take it ([#​73](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/73), [#​87](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/87)).
- `--template` formats JSON output with a Go template, with the functions of `gh` such as `tablerow`, `timeago`, `color` and `hyperlink`. It takes the same `--json` field list; see `gt help formatting` ([#​88](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/88)).
- `gt schema` lists the JSON fields of every command, and a check in CI keeps existing fields from being removed ([#​72](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/72)).
- `GITEA_CLI_ERROR_FORMAT=json` reports failures as JSON on stderr, for scripts and agents ([#​71](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/71)).
- `gt gpg-key` lists, views, adds and deletes GPG keys, and verifies them with `token` and `verify`. `create --signature-file` adds a key that names no activated email address of your account ([#​81](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/81)).
- `gt issue lock`, `unlock`, `pin`, `unpin` and `delete` work on several issues at once. `delete` looks at every issue first and asks once for the batch ([#​82](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/82)).
- `gt pr lock`, `unlock`, `pin`, `unpin` and `delete` select a pull request like `gt pr close`. `delete` takes a branch only for an open pull request, so a closed or merged one needs its number or URL ([#​89](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/89)).
- `gt pr edit` and `gt issue edit` change dependencies in both directions with `--add-blocked-by`, `--remove-blocked-by`, `--add-blocks` and `--remove-blocks`. `gt pr view` and `gt pr edit` output `blocked_by` and `blocks` with `--json` ([#​90](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/90)).
- `--select` on `gt issue list`, `gt pr list`, `gt release list` and `gt repo list` lets you pick an item on a terminal, shows it and runs the action you choose ([#​86](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/86)).
- `gt notification list --all-accounts` lists the notifications of every account you are logged in to ([#​85](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/85)).
- `gt repo license` and `gt repo gitignore` list and print the templates Gitea offers for new repositories, so `gt repo gitignore view Go >> .gitignore` works ([#​83](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/83)).
- `gt project workflow` lists, views, creates, edits, enables, disables and deletes the workflows of a project board. It needs Gitea 29 ([#​61](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/61)).
- `gt admin` adds `user rename`, `user key`, `user badge`, `org list`, `org create`, `cron list`, `cron run` and `email list` ([#​78](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/78)).

##### Internal

- The Windows tests run on every pull request ([#​79](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/79)).
- Update `gitea.dev/sdk` to v1.5.1 ([#​61](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/61)).
- Fix a flaky test that counted requests during concurrent column reads ([#​84](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/pulls/84)).

##### Contributors

- [@​lunny](https://github.com/lunny)
- [@​bircni](https://github.com/bircni)
- [@​silverwind](https://github.com/silverwind)

**Full Changelog**: [v1.0.0...v1.1.0](https://gitea.com/gitea/cli/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0)

</details>

<details>
<summary>mikefarah/yq</summary>

### [`v4.54.3`](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/tag/v4.54.3)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/compare/v4.54.2...v4.54.3)

- Fixed preservation of YAML aliases across documents within the same input stream, without leaking anchors between files ([#​2956](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2956)) Thanks [@​ingydotnet](https://github.com/ingydotnet)
  - Restricted `--split-exp` output paths to the current directory by default. Use `--security-allow-write-any-path` with trusted input to restore the previous behaviour ([#​2965](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2965))
  - Fixed `--inplace` to reject direct updates to read-only files and replace symbolic links instead of modifying their targets.  ([#​2973](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2973))

### [`v4.54.2`](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/tag/v4.54.2)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/compare/v4.54.1...v4.54.2)

- Fixed command injection risk in shell output with `-o=shell -r`: unsafe values are now quoted and a warning is logged. Use `--security-force-never-escape-shell-output` to restore the previous unsafe behaviour (GHSA-h2cv-65fq-jgrp)
  - Fixed YAML structure being changed when assigning head comments ([#​2847](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2847)) Thanks [@​rootsec1](https://github.com/rootsec1)
  - Fixed `ireduce` to run per pipeline input, matching jq's `reduce` behaviour ([#​2869](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2869)) Thanks [@​00200200](https://github.com/00200200)
  - Fixed `map_values` to remove entries when the expression returns nothing ([#​2862](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2862)) Thanks [@​yuefdev](https://github.com/yuefdev)
  - Fixed preservation of comments on TOML inline table values ([#​2879](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2879)) Thanks [@​iamhuman-cheolheelee](https://github.com/iamhuman-cheolheelee)
  - Fixed INI keys containing colons ([#​2886](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2886))
  - Fixed YAML line numbers after header preprocessing ([#​2939](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2939)) Thanks [@​imharjot](https://github.com/imharjot)
  - Fixed an extra leading comment blank line with CRLF input ([#​2856](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2856)) Thanks [@​cestercian](https://github.com/cestercian)
  - Cleaned up failed in-place edits ([#​2920](https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/issues/2920)) Thanks [@​Boulea7](https://github.com/Boulea7)
  - Bumped dependencies

</details>

### HTTP/1 server crash due to MaxBytesReader header race in net/http
[CVE-2026-97054](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-97054) / [GO-2026-6859](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6859)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
For HTTP/1 servers, when MaxBytesReader's limit is exceeded, "Connection: close" header is automatically set without synchronization, which might race with another header being set explicitly in the server handler. As a result, an HTTP/1 server that utilizes MaxBytesReader or MaxBytesHandler can crash due to runtime panic if its handler reads the request body concurrently with writing the response header.

#### Severity
Unknown

#### References
- [https://go.dev/cl/862185](https://go.dev/cl/862185)
- [https://go.dev/issue/82563](https://go.dev/issue/82563)
- [https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM)

This data is provided by [OSV](https://osv.dev/vulnerability/GO-2026-6859) and the [Go Vulnerability Database](https://github.com/golang/vulndb) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://github.com/golang/vulndb#license)).
</details>

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>spf13/pflag (github.com/spf13/pflag)</summary>

### [`v1.1.0`](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/releases/tag/v1.1.0)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/compare/v1.0.10...v1.1.0)

It's been long enough, and enough things have been fixed, that it might be time to release a new version, even if there isn't any particular big new issue to market as the reason for this release.

If you notice anything breaking, it is entirely un-intentional, but you might also have been relying on [undocumented](https://www.hyrumslaw.com/) or [buggy](https://xkcd.com/1172/) behavior. Please file an issue describing what you're doing, how it worked before this release and why it doesn't work anymore, and pin your projects to `v1.0.10` (the latest release before this one) while we decide how to address your concerns.

#### What's Changed

- README: update badges and minor linting fixes by [@​thaJeztah](https://github.com/thaJeztah) in [#​452](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/pull/452)
- Show 'correct' explicit bool value syntax in help by [@​alimpfard](https://github.com/alimpfard) in [#​453](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/pull/453)
- Fix for Go 1.24 by [@​pterjan](https://github.com/pterjan) in [#​460](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/pull/460)
- fix(map): ensure string-to-string flags maintain stable pointers by [@​brandon1024](https://github.com/brandon1024) in [#​457](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/pull/457)
- Fix getFlagType error message by [@​wellitonscheer](https://github.com/wellitonscheer) in [#​462](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/pull/462)
- update actions, and fix linting issues by [@​thaJeztah](https://github.com/thaJeztah) in [#​450](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/pull/450)
- fix: README.md indicating the use of godoc(deprecated) by [@​malklera](https://github.com/malklera) in [#​467](https://github.com/spf13/pflag/pull/467)

### [`v6.1.3`](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/releases/tag/v6.1.3)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/compare/v5.8.9...v6.1.3)

##### Security

- This release addresses [CVE-2026-94603](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/security/advisories/GHSA-2cvf-wqm6-wr9g), where a `podman run` on a checkpoint image (any image with the `io.podman.annotations.checkpoint.runtime.name` annotation) could disable all sandboxing, including sandboxing specified by the user, when the container was created.

##### Breaking Changes

- Removed support for checkpoint images in `podman run` due to serious security concerns with the different security models of running images and running checkpoints. Checkpoints ignore user-specified security configuration and are very difficult to run safely.
